newsitem.title: USA: Wells Fargo says on track to meet goal.
newsitem.headline: Wells Fargo says on track to meet goal.

text.p: Wells Fargo & Co said Tuesday that while it was half-way to its goal of $800 million in gross annual expense reductions, its revenues were affected by runoff in its loan and deposit portfolios.
"We're pleased that we've met our expense reduction target this quarter," said Chairman Paul Hazen in a statement accompanying the company's first quarter earnings.

"We are now half-way to our goal of $800 million in gross annual expense reductions. However, due to runoff in our loan and deposit portfolios we are not where we would like to be with respect to revenue."

The company said that net charge-offs in the first quarter of 1997 totaled $201 million, or 1.23 percent of annualized average loans. The largest category of net charge-offs was credit card loans, totaling $104 million.
At March 31, 1997, the allowance for loan losses equaled 2.94 percent of total loans, Wells Fargo said.
